claim_assessed: For each integer \(n\ge4\), exactly \(12n-36\) labeled optimal size-eleven codes exist for the ternary unordered-multiset channel with two survivors and four-list decoding. Every optimizer is among three one-heavy-only deletions or one of the explicitly enumerated two-heavy replacement families; the capacity eleven is prior knowledge and excluded from novelty.

correctness.rationale: For n>=4 each word has at least one heavy coordinate and only twelve vectors have exactly one. Capacity twelve would force all one-heavy vectors U, violating all mixed-pair lists with load five. If an optimal code has eleven messages and T one-heavy messages, its 3 monochromatic loads satisfy 22-T<=12, so T=10 or 11. T=11 forces removal of one of three full-support B_i; T=10 forces one two-heavy addition, two different heavy-label removals, and the stated mixed-pair cases. The remaining coordinate of the addition is zero or one, yielding three deletion pairs for each of n-3 edge splits or one pair for each n-4 interior splits. All candidate types meet every load by direct incidence inspection. They are disjoint and count 3+3[3(n-3)+(n-4)]=12n-36, including n=4. The packaged whole-simplex and structurally reduced direct enumeration programs replayed with expected output, but the symbolic incidence classification, not the finite outputs, proves the infinite statement.

evidence: The high-list result proves M_3(n,L;2)=floor(3L/2)+6 for L>=5 in its specified length range, with even L>=6 equality structure; the L=4 case does not follow by the stated range.
The general multiset list-capacity plateau theorem proves an equality profile only when 2<=L<=k, and k=2 here, excluding L=4.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither named more general theorem dominates the equality classification: changing the list allowance changes the feasible codebooks and the equality types, and capacity statements alone do not imply optimizer enumeration.

originality.rationale: The relevant first-public 2026 multiset deletion literature introduces and studies this unordered deletion channel but focuses unique decoding and ball geometry. The fully read higher-list published-finding corpus theorem credits the L=4 optimum eleven as known and treats list allowances L>=5, with equality conditions for even L>=6; it neither counts nor classifies the eleven-word L=4 optimizers. The fully read general low-list theorem has L<=survivor count, hence L<=2 here. Direct published-finding corpus queries and source/alias/parameter and code searches did not surface an equivalent structural L=4 optimizer census. The asserted novelty excludes eleven-message capacity and consists of the explicit exhaustive two-type classification and linear count; possible unindexed earlier same-subject results remain a priority risk.
residual_risks: The previously known L=4 cardinality result is cited secondhand by the high-list theorem, but its original standalone source could not be located directly by semantic or title search; a hitherto unindexed stronger equality classification remains possible.
Complete global literature coverage cannot be inferred from limited search; originality is best-of-knowledge, not independent certification.

value.rationale: Capacity alone does not identify any or all optimal codebooks. The theorem classifies all optimal designs in a natural ternary unordered-multiset list-decoding channel for every length, detects the two qualitatively different equality structures (pure one-heavy deletions and a single two-heavy replacement), and counts their distinct labeled realizations 12n-36. This is an all-length exact structural equality classification with immediate interpretation as design diversity and reproducible finite tests, not a parameter-renaming or a routine one-off numerical table.
